MUSICAL INTERVALS AS OMEGA STATES
Consonance = high Omega (simple integer ratios) · Dissonance = low Omega (complex ratios) · Music is T×S=C made audible
The Core Principle
Simple integer ratios = high order = high Omega = consonant. The ratio of two frequencies is the J/S ratio in sound. 2:1 (octave) is maximally ordered. 45:32 (tritone) is maximally entropic. The ear hears Omega directly.
The Tritone — Diabolus in Musica
The tritone (45:32, “the Devil in Music”) = J/S=−0.25 (Anger range). Medieval composers banned it because it is literally the most entropic interval available in Western music. It was forbidden because it makes the listener’s system drop below J/S=0.

The Perfect Fifth (3:2) = J/S=126.7 (Near Timeless range). This is why Pythagorean tuning based entirely on fifths feels “pure” — it is operating at H=800, above the Near Timeless threshold. Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier tempered the fifth to make all keys usable, trading some Near Timeless purity for accessibility.
Resolution = Omega Optimization
Musical resolution — moving from dissonance to consonance — is dΩ/dt > 0 in sound. The tension of a suspended fourth resolving to a third is the system moving from J/S=46 to J/S=7. Every resolution in music is a metemphysical ordering event. The ear craves resolution because it craves Omega.

432 Hz vs 440 Hz — The Order Debate
A = 432 Hz
432 = 8 × 54 = 16 × 27 = 432. Embedded in natural cycles: 432,000 miles = radius of the sun; 432 = 2&sup4; × 3³ — deeply embedded in integer relationships. Verdi’s pitch. Considered the “natural” tuning. In Metemphysics: A=432 produces integer frequency relationships across the entire instrument, maximising interval Omega throughout.
A = 440 Hz
440 = 8 × 55 = 440. Standardised in 1939. While convenient for industrial production, 440 creates slightly more complex ratios across the instrument. The debate continues. In Metemphysics: the question is which tuning minimises S across the full instrument, maximising mean interval Omega. 432 has stronger structural claim.

Pythagorean Tuning & The Music of the Spheres

Pythagoras (570–495 BCE) discovered that musical intervals correspond to simple integer ratios. More importantly, he proposed that the planets produce music through their orbital relationships — the “Music of the Spheres.” In Metemphysics: orbital resonances are T×S=C relationships. Planetary orbits in integer ratios (as Jupiter and Saturn approach 5:2 resonance) are the universe maintaining high Omega at the cosmic scale. The Music of the Spheres is T×S=C expressed as gravitational harmony. Pythagoras was not wrong. He lacked the equation.

Orbital resonance = J/S optimisation at planetary scale = T × S = C in gravitational form
